subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which remaining tool-overhead reduction should OpenClaw make next, and should it be a default-compatible core change, an opt-in config/API surface, or a Tool Search/plugin-SDK design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix choices change provider-facing payloads, prompt defaults, channel compatibility, cron behavior, and possibly public plugin/config contracts, so maintainer product/API intent is required before implementation.

options.title: Sequence Compatible Core Reductions
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and land small default-compatible reductions first, with narrow follow-up issues for public API or config additions.

options.title: Promote Lazy SDK/API Work
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98300 or a successor the next canonical implementation path for deferred tool schemas, accepting a public plugin API design step.

options.title: Defer To Existing Tool Search
options.body: Treat Tool Search directory mode as the supported answer for large catalogs and close or narrow only the parts maintainers do not plan to optimize in core.

recommendation.title: Sequence Compatible Core Reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and land small default-compatible reductions first, with narrow follow-up issues for public API or config additions.

likelyOwner.reason: The central prompt/tool-schema code history and prior maintainer-side review context make steipete the strongest available owner for this product/API sequencing decision.
